chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph says the output is a single comment-free line, so each of `eval "$(...)"`, the unquoted `eval $(...)`, and `source <(...)` registers it, after documenting fish as one of the supported shells. Fish does not support POSIX-style `$()` command substitution or `<(...)` process substitution; `source <(ddflow completion fish)` in `config.fish` is a parse error, not a registration. A fish user following this blanket claim can end up with an invalid startup line that never registers completion.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/completion.md:11

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper claims to check that the script “really registers the engine’s completer,” but it only checks that a needle appears somewhere in the text. For `shell="bash"`, a script containing just `complete -F _python_argcomplete ddflow` is syntactically valid, comment-free, word-join-safe, and contains `_python_argcomplete`, so the conformance test passes even though no `_python_argcomplete` function is defined and invoking completion would produce no answers. The same weakness applies to zsh (`compdef _python_argcomplete ddflow` without defining the function) and fish (`complete -c ddflow -f -a '(__fish_ddflow_complete)'` without defining `__fish_ddflow_complete`). The previous anchored definition check would have rejected such placeholders; this change reintroduces the possibility of a registration that never answers.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:_registers_a_completer

chunk_findings.detail: The shell subprocess environment is not isolated from inherited shell startup variables. For bash, `_run` invokes `bash -c`, and non-interactive bash sources the file named by `BASH_ENV` before executing the test script. The `shim` fixture only overrides `PATH` and `HOME`, so if the surrounding environment has `BASH_ENV` set to a script that defines a `ddflow` shell function, that function shadows the temporary `ddflow` shim. For example, with `BASH_ENV=/tmp/preload.sh` containing `ddflow() { :; }`, the command substitution `$(ddflow completion bash)` in `test_bash_registers_under_every_spelling` produces no output, no completion is registered, and `complete -p ddflow` leaves stdout empty, causing the test to fail even though the activation text itself is correct. Conversely, a `BASH_ENV` script that pre-registers a `_python_argcomplete` completion could make the test pass even if the activation output is broken.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:35 (`shim` fixture / `_run`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper claims to check that the text “really registers” a completer, but it only does a substring search. Given `completion_shell.for_shell("bash")` returning `# _python_argcomplete` (or `echo _python_argcomplete >&2`), `bash -n` accepts the text and `_registers_a_completer("bash", text)` returns True, so the conformance test asserts registration even though no `complete` command is present. The same applies to zsh and to fish: a fish script containing only `function __fish_ddflow_complete; end` (no `complete -c ddflow ...`) would also pass. This reintroduces the false positive the removed `_activation_defined` regex explicitly guarded against (“an echo or comment that merely mentions the name does not pass”).

chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph makes a blanket claim that the activation output is usable through `eval "$(...)"`, unquoted `eval $(...)`, and `source <(...)`, immediately after listing fish as a supported shell. chunk_findings.detail: `test_zsh_registers_under_every_spelling` probes the registered zsh function with `"REG=${{_comps[ddflow]}}"`. In zsh, the associative-array element expansion is `${_comps[ddflow]}`; the doubled-brace form is not a valid parameter expansion. When zsh is installed, the probe line aborts with a bad substitution (or otherwise fails to emit the expected value), so `probe.stdout` does not contain `REG=_python_argcomplete` even if `ddflow completion zsh` correctly registered `_python_argcomplete`. Thus every zsh registration test fails on a normal zsh environment, and on environments without zsh the tests skip instead of validating the intended behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:76

chunk_findings.detail: The helper accepts the zsh `compdef _python_argcomplete ddflow` registration string for every shell, not just zsh. For `shell="bash"`, a text such as `"_python_argcomplete() { :; }\ncompdef _python_argcomplete ddflow\n"` satisfies the function-definition regex and the `registers` check even though it contains no `complete -F _python_argcomplete ddflow` and therefore does not register a bash completion. The conformance test would pass a bash activation script that only contains a zsh registration, contrary to its stated purpose of asserting shell-specific registration.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:_registers_a_completer

chunk_findings.detail: The bash/zsh function-definition regex `(?:^|[;\n]|\\n)_python_argcomplete\(\) \{` is too strict about whitespace. It rejects valid shell definitions such as `; _python_argcomplete() { :; }` (space after the semicolon) or `_python_argcomplete(){ :; }` (no space before the brace). Given a correctly registering script using either form, `_registers_a_completer` returns False and the conformance test fails even though the shell would register the completer.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:_registers_a_completer

chunk_findings.detail: Unquoted `eval $(ddflow completion zsh)` never registers on default zsh. The line is split on spaces and each word is pathname-expanded before `eval` rejoins them; `_quote` only escapes `\`, `'`, newlines, tabs and multi-space runs, and the boot prefix is not quoted at all. The word `$+functions[compdef]` contains an unmatched `[compdef]` glob, and zsh NOMATCH (on by default) aborts with "no matches found" so the `eval $'...'` registration never runs. The same split exposes `?`/`*`/`[` inside argcomplete shellcode (for example `$?`), so bash corrupts the script whenever the cwd has a matching name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_shell.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: `test_without_argcomplete_one_harmless_line` does not observe a missing `argcomplete`. It only sets `sys.modules["argcomplete"]` to `None`, then asserts one trailing newline and the substring `argcomplete`. The success line already satisfies both (`_python_argcomplete`, one `\n`). With `argcomplete` installed, `importlib.util.find_spec("argcomplete")` still finds the on-disk package, and a `for_shell` that never re-imports after this monkeypatch still returns the success line, so the test passes without ever exercising the no-argcomplete path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:108

chunk_findings.detail:
When `argcomplete` is not installed, `for_shell` returns `_message(shell)`. `_NO_ENGINE` contains single quotes, but `_message` wraps it in single-quoted shell strings without escaping those quotes. For bash/zsh, the generated line is:

`printf '%s\n' 'ddflow: shell completion needs the 'argcomplete' package (pip install argcomplete)' >&2`

When this is `eval`-ed (in any of the supported forms), the quotes terminate early and `printf` receives three arguments after the format, so it prints three stderr lines instead of the intended one-line message. For fish, line 53 has the same unescaped-single-quote problem, so the `echo` line is not the intended correctly quoted message. This contradicts the documented “one harmless line” fallback and can pollute or break the activation path when the optional dependency is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_shell.py:28,53-54

chunk_findings.detail: The generated `ddflow` shim uses an unquoted shebang: `f"#!{sys.executable}\n..."`. If `sys.executable` contains spaces, or is longer than the OS shebang argument limit, invoking the shim fails before Python runs. For example, if the test runs under `[REDACTED:path] Project/venv/bin/python`, the kernel parses the shebang interpreter as `[REDACTED:path]` and the remaining text as an argument, so `ddflow completion zsh` cannot execute. Consequently `eval $(ddflow completion zsh)`, `eval "$(ddflow completion zsh)"`, and `source <(ddflow completion zsh)` all fail even though `CS.for_shell` itself is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:shim

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion is only a substring/regex search and is not anchored to executable shell statements, so a comment-only or echo-only activation script can satisfy it. For example, for `shell="zsh"`, if `scripts.for_shell("zsh")` returned `# _python_argcomplete() { true; }; compdef _python_argcomplete ddflow\ntrue`, the syntax check passes, `defined` matches after the space in the comment, and `register in text` is true, but the zsh file registers no completer. The same applies to fish: `# function __fish_ddflow_complete; end; complete --command ddflow --arguments '(__fish_ddflow_complete)'\ntrue` matches both searches even though the registration line is commented out. chunk_findings.detail:
When `argcomplete` is not installed, `for_shell` returns `_message(shell)`. `_NO_ENGINE` contains single quotes, but `_message` wraps it in single-quoted shell strings without escaping those quotes. For bash/zsh, the generated line is:

`printf '%s\n' 'ddflow: shell completion needs the 'argcomplete' package (pip install argcomplete)' >&2`

When this is `eval`-ed (in any of the supported forms), the quotes terminate early and `printf` receives three arguments after the format, so it prints three stderr lines instead of the intended one-line message. For fish, line 53 has the same unescaped-single-quote problem, so the `echo` line is not the intended correctly quoted message. This contradicts the documented “one harmless line” fallback and can pollute or break the activation path when the optional dependency is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion_shell.py:28,53-54

chunk_findings.detail: The generated `ddflow` shim uses an unquoted shebang: `f"#!{sys.executable}\n..."`. If `sys.executable` contains spaces, or is longer than the OS shebang argument limit, invoking the shim fails before Python runs. For example, if the test runs under `[REDACTED:path] Project/venv/bin/python`, the kernel parses the shebang interpreter as `[REDACTED:path]` and the remaining text as an argument, so `ddflow completion zsh` cannot execute. Consequently `eval $(ddflow completion zsh)`, `eval "$(ddflow completion zsh)"`, and `source <(ddflow completion zsh)` all fail even though `CS.for_shell` itself is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:shim

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion is only a substring/regex search and is not anchored to executable shell statements, so a comment-only or echo-only activation script can satisfy it. For example, for `shell="zsh"`, if `scripts.for_shell("zsh")` returned `# _python_argcomplete() { true; }; compdef _python_argcomplete ddflow\ntrue`, the syntax check passes, `defined` matches after the space in the comment, and `register in text` is true, but the zsh file registers no completer. The same applies to fish: `# function __fish_ddflow_complete; end; complete --command ddflow --arguments '(__fish_ddflow_complete)'\ntrue` matches both searches even though the registration line is commented out. Thus the test can pass a placeholder that never answers, contrary to its stated purpose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_conformance.py:_registers_a_completer

chunk_findings.detail: The new real-shell test passes `dict(os.environ)` directly to `_run`, while the surrounding helper deliberately strips `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, and `ZDOTDIR` from the environment used for shell probes. Given a developer environment where `BASH_ENV=/tmp/exit.sh` and `/tmp/exit.sh` contains `exit 3`, `bash -c 'printf ... >&2'` sources `BASH_ENV` before executing the completion message line, so `probe.returncode` becomes 3 and this test fails even though the completion output itself is valid. The zsh parametrization can fail the same way if `ZDOTDIR` points to a `.zshenv` that exits non-zero.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_completion_activation.py:test_without_argcomplete_line_runs_and_says_so

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten shim embeds `ROOT` inside a single-quoted `-c` string and inside a double-quoted Python string literal without escaping quote characters. If the repository path contains an apostrophe, e.g. `[REDACTED:path]'s/ddflow`, the generated shim contains `exec "/usr/bin/python" -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "[REDACTED:path]'s/ddflow"); ...' "$@"`, which is invalid POSIX shell because the apostrophe in the path terminates the single-quoted `-c` argument early. Invoking the shim then fails before Python can produce completion output, so the shim-based activation tests fail on a valid repository path.
